name: QEMU linux-user arm: kernel commpage mapped MAP_FIXED at guest 0xffff0000 (COMMPAGE 0xffff0f00 rounded down to the host page)
required_postconditions: the mapping lands at exactly g2h_untagged(COMMPAGE & -host_page_size), i.e. guest_base + 0xffff0000
the page is later mprotect'ed to PROT_READ, so it must survive a protection downgrade in place
COMMPAGE + TARGET_PAGE_SIZE - 1 <= arm_max_reserved_va() == 0xffffffff, which is why 32-bit ARM overrides MAX_RESERVED_VA

failure_sink.description: mmap failure is perror('Allocating guest commpage') + exit(EXIT_FAILURE) at lines 233-234. A mapping that succeeds at the WRONG address returns false (line 236), and the caller then hits g_assert_not_reached() at linux-user/elfload.c:775 - a fatal assert, because probe_guest_base already proved the range was free.

source_locations.symbol: (commpage < reserved_va ? MAP_FIXED : MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE) - MAP_FIXED is used when the page is inside QEMU's own reservation
mprotect(addr, host_page_size, PROT_READ) after writing the helper version word
arm_max_reserved_va returns 0xfffffffful with the comment 'We need to be able to map the commpage.'

extraction_limitations: size 4096 is qemu_real_host_page_size() on the probe host, not a source constant; the source uses the runtime host page size.

the address is a GUEST address. The host address actually requested is guest_base + 0xffff0000; guest_base is 0 only when the identity map succeeded. Modelling it as a host address is exact only for the identity case.

x_campaign.rationale: 0xffff0000 is a page-aligned address well inside the x86-64 Linux user address space and above mmap_min_addr; nothing normally occupies 4 GiB - 64 KiB, and MAP_FIXED makes placement unconditional anyway.
